stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context for robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves a three-order-of-magnitude increase in context length without increasing inference latency.
Enables new capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation and on-the-fly policy improvement.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies

Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a key technical achievement.
Unlocks advanced capabilities such as one-shot in-context imitation and on-the-fly policy improvement in robotics.

stories.author: wp2shell.com via Helithumper
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability, 'wp2shell', has been discovered in WordPress core.

This represents a high-severity security flaw impacting a massive portion of the web.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The performance gain is achieved by utilizing Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs.
Users benefit from faster response times and reduced memory consumption.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these AI agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating active development and adoption of Apple's ML framework.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI agents entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Google-backed satellites for wildfire detection launch as smoke chokes US, Canada
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Google-backed FireSat satellites are being deployed to enhance wildfire detection capabilities.
The new satellite system is designed to identify wildfires that existing satellite technology often misses.
The deployment is timely, addressing the critical issue of smoke and wildfires affecting the US and Canada.

stories.title: San Francisco orders Apple, Google to remove nudify apps from app stores
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: San Francisco has mandated that Apple and Google remove 'nudify' applications from their respective app stores.
The regulatory action targets apps that use manipulative design patterns to influence user behavior.
The ruling implies significant potential revenue loss for Apple and Google from these specific types of applications.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
The attack vector moves beyond limited, established datasets (like Wikipedia) to target the large-scale, heterogeneous corpora used in modern LLM training.
The study highlights the difficulty in detecting and mitigating these poisoning attacks, especially when considering data curation pipelines.

stories.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
stories.author: Eli Shlizerman
bullet_points: Introduces SceneBind, an omni-modal representation designed to integrate vision, audio, and language.
Addresses a key limitation in existing models by explicitly incorporating 3D spatial understanding alongside semantic information.
Represents scenes as semantic-spatial entities, combining global embeddings with object-centric slots.

stories.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
stories.author: Stefan Feuerriegel
bullet_points: Introduces AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system designed for automated meta-analysis.
Addresses the current bottleneck of manual and difficult-to-scale quantitative evidence synthesis in research.
The system can take a natural language research question and autonomously handle literature searching, screening, and data extraction.

stories.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
stories.author: Ke Xu
bullet_points: Investigates the critical gap between text-level safety and physical safety when LLMs control embodied agents.
Demonstrates that 'physical danger' (PD) and 'content danger' (CD) are distinct, separable safety signals within LLM representations.
Uses advanced techniques like hidden-state direction analysis on models like Qwen2.5 to probe this physical risk space.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
Previous poisoning research was limited to established, small-scale data sources (like Wikipedia) and ignored data curation pipelines.
The study proves that poisoning attacks are feasible across the large-scale and heterogeneous corpora typical of modern LLM training.

stories.title: Qwen3.8 is launching and going open-weight soon
stories.author: nh43215rgb
bullet_points: Qwen3.8 is on the verge of a launch.
The model is slated to become open-weight soon.
This signals a significant update in the large language model landscape.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models and hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing Claude Code's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Dave Eggers told OpenAI staff  that ChatGPT was ‘silencing an entire generation’
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Author Dave Eggers expressed concern to OpenAI staff that ChatGPT is 'silencing an entire generation.'
The discussion took place during a talk given by Eggers to approximately 200 OpenAI employees.
Eggers is a prominent writer and advocate for the arts, lending weight to his critique of generative AI's impact.

stories.title: Will AI fix prior authorization—or make it worse?
stories.author: Joshua Cohen, Undark Magazine
bullet_points: A government pilot program is testing the use of Artificial Intelligence in insurance coverage decisions.
The article explores the potential dual impact of AI on the prior authorization process: improvement versus complication.
This touches upon the intersection of AI adoption, healthcare administration, and regulatory oversight.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual and time-consuming process of editing scientific diagrams during paper revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex, heterogeneous visual grammar of scientific infographics (schematics, plots, arrows, etc.).

stories.title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents
stories.author: Yaron Singer
bullet_points: The paper introduces a new evaluation paradigm for AI security agents that moves beyond simple success rates.
It emphasizes 'cost-aware' evaluation, recognizing that operational security tasks consume computational budget (inference, tool calls, etc.).
The methodology is tested on offensive Cybench challenges and defensive Splunk BOTS v1.

stories.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces SearchOS, a system-level multi-agent framework designed to improve open-domain information seeking.
Addresses a key limitation in current LLM agents: getting stuck in repetitive search loops when initial queries fail.
Focuses on enhancing task progress tracking and search efficiency in complex, multi-step information retrieval tasks.

stories.title: teLLMe Why (Ain't Nothing but a Jam): Exploratory Causal Analysis of Urban Driving Data
stories.author: Jorge Ortiz
bullet_points: Introduces 'teLLMe,' a system designed for exploratory causal analysis of urban driving data.
Addresses the challenge of answering causal questions (e.g., impact of rain) using purely observational traffic data.
Combines causal structure learning with structured event tables derived from dashcam annotations.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on pre-training corpus priorities, leading to suboptimal performance for later-added languages.
Adding new languages can cause increased tokenization overhead (more tokens per word), negatively impacting latency, compute, and energy use.
The issue is exacerbated in compact models where the overhead of large vocabularies (embedding/LM-head matrices) is more significant compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Xuan Luo
bullet_points: Addresses the real-time constraint challenge in dynamic novel view synthesis from streaming video.
Identifies the computational bottleneck of traditional Test-Time Training (TTT) due to required gradient-based memory updates.
Proposes an 'Online Neural Space Time Memory' to overcome the trade-off between long-horizon memory and real-time performance.

stories.title: Mutable Low-Rank Sketches for Retrain-Free Recommendation
stories.author: Nick Clayton
bullet_points: Addresses the 'embedding staleness' bottleneck in two-stage recommendation systems.
Introduces 'mutable sketches' using a KP-tree to store user preferences efficiently.
Allows for on-the-fly embedding updates upon new user ratings without requiring full retraining.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource usage.
The issue is more critical for compact models, as large vocabulary matrices are a significant overhead compared to massive cloud models.

stories.title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
stories.author: Subodh Kalia
bullet_points: Introduces NeuronSoup, a novel neural computation architecture that moves away from traditional synchronous, layer-by-layer processing.
Employs asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation through a pool of shared neurons, allowing continuous-valued signals to traverse variable paths.
Notably, the architecture operates without relying on backpropagation, suggesting a potential shift in training paradigms for neural networks.

stories.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
stories.author: Xinchao Wang
bullet_points: World-Action Models (WAMs) are a promising new paradigm for embodied control by coupling action generation with future world prediction.
The paper introduces 'BadWAM' to demonstrate that the assumption of inherent robustness and safety in WAMs is fragile.
BadWAM provides a unified framework for modeling and evaluating the potential failures in these advanced control models.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: Introduces SciDiagramEdit, a system designed to automate the editing of scientific diagrams.
The system allows authors to modify figures (relabeling, rearranging, restyling) using natural language instructions.
Addresses the complexity of scientific figures, which are dense infographics composed of heterogeneous visual elements.

stories.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
stories.author: Shubham Chatterjee
bullet_points: Traditional retrieval system evaluation (static usefulness) fails when LLMs act as multi-step search agents.
The utility of a retrieved document in agentic search depends on its potential to enable future actions, not just answering the current query.
The research highlights a critical gap between static document relevance and dynamic, multi-turn reasoning in AI agents.

stories.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
stories.author: Steven A. Hicks
bullet_points: The research focuses on designing trustworthy and interpretable multimodal Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems for healthcare applications.
The study uses a GI endoscopy case study from MediaEval Medico 2025 to evaluate nine existing systems.
While parameter-efficient adaptation improves performance, it doesn't guarantee faithful or complete clinical reasoning in the AI answers.

stories.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations
stories.author: Bowen Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces TikStance, a new multimodal and hierarchical dataset specifically designed for stance detection in political conversations on TikTok.
Addresses the current gap in computational analysis by combining audiovisual information with conversational context from short-video platforms.
The dataset is focused on the 2024 U.S. election cycle, covering discussions around major political figures.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource usage.
The issue is more critical for compact models, as large models can absorb a broader vocabulary due to parameter distribution.

stories.title: Expanding the Lexicon of Ge'ez Based African Languages: A Comparative Study of Amharic and Tigrinya
stories.author: Wolfgang Nejdl
bullet_points: Addresses the performance degradation of Multilingual Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs) on low-resource, non-Latin-script African languages.
Introduces VEXMLM, a vocabulary-extended variant of XLM-R specifically designed for Ge'ez-script languages (Amharic and Tigrinya).
Evaluates the model's effectiveness across 19 African languages, aiming to mitigate high Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) rates caused by Latin-centric tokenizers.

stories.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Philipp Krähenbühl
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
A key difficulty in current approaches is the intractability of log-likelihood estimation in MDLMs.
The proposed method accounts for the sequential nature of unmasking decisions during MDLM generation, improving upon existing token-prediction-only approximations.

stories.title: Speech Recognition and TTS in less than 500kb
stories.author: petewarden
bullet_points: Achieving speech recognition and Text-to-Speech (TTS) in a very small footprint (<500kb).
This suggests significant progress in model compression and efficient on-device AI.
The small size makes deployment on resource-constrained devices highly feasible.

stories.title: Optimizing RAG at Scale: Chunking, Retrieval, and the Bayesian Search That Cut Latency 40%
stories.author: imus_d7584cbc8ee9b0336256
bullet_points: Focuses on optimizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for large-scale deployment.
Addresses key technical challenges including chunking strategies and retrieval efficiency.
Highlights the implementation of a Bayesian Search method that resulted in a 40% latency reduction.

stories.title: Optimizing RAG at Scale: Chunking, Retrieval, and the Bayesian Search That Cut Latency 40%
stories.author: imus_d7584cbc8ee9b0336256
bullet_points: Focuses on optimizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for large-scale deployment.
Addresses key technical challenges including chunking strategies and retrieval efficiency.
Highlights the implementation of a Bayesian Search method that resulted in a 40% latency reduction.

stories.title: Building Production-Grade LLM Evaluation Pipelines: From Vibes to Metrics
stories.author: imus_d7584cbc8ee9b0336256
bullet_points: Focuses on the practical engineering challenge of moving LLM evaluation from subjective assessment ('vibes') to quantifiable metrics.
Addresses the need for robust, production-grade pipelines for Large Language Model testing.
Relevant to ML engineers and AI practitioners building enterprise-level LLM applications.

stories.title: Personal AI Should Ask Before It Remembers
stories.author: diaryvault
bullet_points: Focuses on building a personal AI memory layer using Python.
Emphasizes user control by implementing features like persistent drafts and explicit human approval.
Contributes to the growing trend of making AI systems more transparent and controllable.
